title: NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) — Premium Received but Not Owed on Cancellation
content:
On the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own), premium payments that the cancelled policy does not owe — payments posted for a term that never began, and payments above a returned term's charges — are added to the cancellation refund.

**Rule.** The premium received but not owed is settled as follows: when a payment has been posted for a term that has not yet begun, it is that whole payment plus the amount by which the payments posted for each term the cancellation returns exceed that term's charges; when the payments posted for a term the cancellation returns exceed that term's charges, it is that excess; otherwise there is none. Whichever case applies, the premium received but not owed is reduced, never below zero, by the amount by which the refunds already disbursed on the policy exceed the premium credits booked on it other than cancellation credits.

The terms the cancellation returns are the current term and, when the cancellation took effect before the current term start, the term before it.

## Input — judgement — output

| Premium account shows | Premium received but not owed |
|---|---|
| a payment posted for a term not yet begun | that whole payment plus each returned term's payments above its charges |
| no such payment; a returned term's payments above its charges | that excess |
| neither | none |

Then: less the refunds already disbursed in excess of the non-cancellation premium credits, never below zero.

## Case (hypothetical)

A renewal payment of 3,900.00 posted for a term starting next month; current term payments 4,100.00 against charges of 4,000.00; no earlier refunds: 3,900.00 plus 100.00, which is 4,000.00.
